_comment: Which rail each capacitor sits on, and what that rail runs at.
The rated voltage is NOT here -- it is read from the parts list
at run time, so a corrected BOM corrects this too.
source: 'schematic' means the net was traced on the Chapter 7
sheet cited in the note; 'inferred' means it was deduced from
the rails present at that slot and has not been read off a
schematic. appliedV: null means the rail was never traced --
shown as unknown rather than assumed safe.
railClass is how much energy is behind the rail, which decides
what a shorted part does: A is an unfused 3 A rail with a
6600 uF reservoir, C is fused, E is a floating common.

C9.note: *** WORST IN INSTRUMENT, AND CONFIRMED SO *** — re-verified 2026-08 by the tantalum audit, which expected to find an error here and did not. Figure 7-19 sheet 2 of 3 (Ch7 PDF page 75), zone around the SC+ (PG2D8) arrow: C9 (15 µF, '+' plate on the SC+ side) sits directly in parallel with VR15 and with C8 (0.22 µF), between the SC+ node and the amplifier OUT node. R19, 68 kΩ 1 W, feeds that node from the high side, so VR15 is a working shunt regulator carrying current continuously, not a fault clamp that idles: SC+ really does stand 18 V above OUT whenever the amplifier is powered. VR15's parts-list row is ZENER,UNCOMP,18.0V,5%,7.0MA,0.4W, so the node is 17.1-18.9 V over tolerance, i.e. 86-95 % of C9's 20 V rating. Both parts lists give C9 as CAP,TA,15UF,+-20%,20V (Fluke stock 807610) — the same stock number A8 fits at 5 V — so the rating is not a transcription error and the rail is not a mis-trace. This is simply a part Fluke ran at 90 % of rating. Replace it first, and fit at least 35 V; a 50 V part if the case size allows, since Vishay's MnO2 table asks for more derating above 15 V, not less.

C21.note: Re-verified 2026-08. Figure 7-19 sheet 2 of 3 (Ch7 PDF page 75), beside the SC- (PG2D8) arrow: C21 (15 µF, '+' plate on the PACOM side) is in parallel with VR18 and C20 (0.22 µF) between PACOM and the SC- node, fed from -PA by R57, 68 kΩ 1 W. Same shunt-regulator topology as C9/VR15 on the positive side, but the zener here is a different value — VR18's parts-list row is ZENER,UNCOMP,15.0V,5%,8.5MA,0.4W against VR15's 18.0 V — so the negative half genuinely runs 3 V lower than the positive half. That asymmetry is real, not a misread: it is why C9 lands at 90 % of rating and its identical twin C21 at 75 %. 15 V +/-5 % is 14.25-15.75 V, i.e. 71-79 % of C21's 20 V rating. Replace it with C9 and fit the same 35 V or better.

C45.net: Across Q38 (TIP32) emitter-base — +8RLH emitter stub to heater hybrid pin 6
C45.note: CORRECTED 2026-08 by the tantalum audit; was 20 V (57 % of a 35 V part) on the +8RLH rail. Re-read at 400 dpi on Figure 7-19 sheet 3 of 3 (Ch7 PDF page 76), in the hybrid heater control block beside P702: C45 is drawn vertically from the +8RLH stub down to the line that leaves Q38's base bar and runs to the HEATER CONTROL (50C) hybrid pin 6. Q38's emitter is that same +8RLH stub. So C45 is the pass transistor's base-emitter bypass, not a rail decoupler, and it sees V_EB — about 0.7-0.8 V while the heater is driven, zero when it is not. It is the exact twin of A7's C15 (which had the same error), and of A11 C19/C20 and A15 C14/C19, which are the same 2.2 uF part across the same TIP32 E-B junction. 2 % of a 35 V rating; leave it alone. The +8RLH rail's own spec (A17 F1 3.15 A, fault code 3609 accepts +10 to +20 V) is not what stands across this part.
